messages:
John (ACME): Hey team — our staging org just ran out of monthly credits at 2026-03-31 23:00 PDT (we're on Pacific). We expected reset at midnight UTC. Can you confirm when monthly quotas actually reset? We got 429s and a bunch of client errors right after.

Maya (Support): Thanks for the ping, John. Sorry for the disruption. Quick questions: is the org timezone set to Pacific in the billing console? And did you see the quota depletion notification from quota-bot in the org channel?

John (ACME): I checked billing console — it shows "Billing cycle: 1st of month, timezone: PT". quota-bot posted this message to our org channel at 2026-03-31 23:02 PDT: "Your org has consumed 100% of monthly credits. Requests will be rate limited until next refill.". But our engineers saw 429s at ~23:05 PDT, then another burst of errors at 00:05 PDT (which makes it ambiguous).

quota-bot: Your org (acme-staging) has exhausted monthly credits (100%). Requests that exceed quota will receive 429 until next refill or top-up. See /orgs/acme-staging/billing for details.

Nina (Support): John's right — the messages line up. Can you paste a couple of example request IDs that returned 429 so we can trace logs? Also, did you have any scheduled batch jobs around that hour?

John (ACME): Request IDs: req_8a2f1c, req_8a2f7b. We had a nightly batch at 22:50 PDT that does bulk embedding (spiky token usage).

Maya (Support): Copying Lina from eng-oncall for logs and to confirm reset semantics. @Lina can you check whether the refill is anchored to org timezone or UTC and whether there are known DST/offset issues?

Lina (eng-oncall): Thanks @Maya — looking. Short answer: monthly quota refills are anchored to the org's billing timezone setting, but there was an edge case where DST transitions could cause a 1-hour offset in the notification vs actual refill timestamp for orgs created before 2024-11-01. I'm pulling logs for acme-staging now.

ops-bot: Ingestion trace: req_8a2f1c -> 2026-03-31T22:52:13-07:00 (PDT) tokens=1,250,345; req_8a2f7b -> 2026-03-31T22:55:02-07:00 tokens=2,012,900; quota consumed to 100% at 2026-03-31T23:01:09-07:00.

Lina (eng-oncall): From logs: org hit 100% at 23:01 PDT. Automatic refill job scheduled for 2026-04-01T00:00:00 in the org billing timezone (PT). Refill job started at 00:00 PT and completed at 00:00:10 PT. However I see the rate limiter continued rejecting some requests until 00:05 PT because of in-flight request accounting and a lag in cache invalidation on the global rate-limiter. That explains the 00:05 spike you saw.

John (ACME): Ok that makes sense — but why did quota-bot post the depletion at 23:02 and then we saw 429s until 00:05? If refill happened at 00:00 PT, shouldn't things be back to normal immediately?

Raj (Billing): Quick clarifying note: quota depletion notifications are triggered when the accounting ledger marks available credits <= 0. The refill is a separate scheduled job. There can be a race where the notification goes out immediately on depletion but legacy caches for token buckets take a few minutes to sync. We're working to shorten that window.

Maya (Support): Actionable short term: 1) If you need immediate relief we can process a one-time top-up to cover the in-flight spike (we can add X credits now). 2) Engineering is going to invalidate the rate-limiter cache for acme-staging to stop lingering 429s in this case. Would you like us to apply the top-up while we do the cache invalidation?

John (ACME): Yes please do both. We want to avoid failing nightly batches. Also can you document the repro steps so our infra knows how to avoid this?

Lina (eng-oncall): Repro notes (for your infra/playbook):

1) Setup org with billing timezone = PT.
2) Simulate heavy token consumption just before local midnight (e.g., run two large embedding batches within 15 minutes).
3) Observe ledger hits 0 -> quota-bot posts depletion immediately.
4) Refill job runs at 00:00 local time, but rate-limiter cache may still show exhausted for ~5 minutes if there are high in-flight request volumes.

Examples (curl) to check quota status and request tracing:

# check org billing & timezone
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/orgs/acme-staging/billing

# check quota ledger snapshot
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/orgs/acme-staging/usage/ledger?at=2026-03-31T23:00:00-07:00

# check request log by request id
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/requests/req_8a2f1c

Lina (eng-oncall): Mitigations we suggest for customers who run heavy nightly batches around local midnight:
- Shift large batches 30+ minutes earlier or later to avoid the refill window.
- Enable soft-topup policy (auto-add credits up to N) in the billing console — that can keep jobs running during brief refill race windows.
- For production-grade, consider Redwood Dedicated or Reserved capacity to avoid per-token exhaustion.

Raj (Billing): I've queued a one-time top-up of 5M tokens to acme-staging account; should reflect in ledger within ~1 minute. Also flagged the org for priority cache invalidation.

ops-bot: Cache invalidation triggered for org acme-staging at 2026-04-01T00:01:12-07:00.

Maya (Support): Confirming the top-up and invalidation are done. Can you re-run the batch or try a test request and paste a request id if you still see 429s?

John (ACME): Ran a quick test at 00:02 PT: req_c3d2b1 returned 200, tokens=3,200. Then at 00:04 another test req_c3d2b6 returned 429 briefly but immediately retried and succeeded at 00:06. Looks good now. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Maya (Support): Great — closing loop: root cause = hit 100% before local midnight + short (few-minute) cache sync lag in rate limiter during high in-flight volume. Short-term remediation we applied = one-time top-up + cache invalidation. Long-term: engineering will ship a fix to reduce cache lag and improve notification messaging to show expected refill wall-clock time. I'll follow up in ~48h once the eng fix lands and we validate with a canary run.

John (ACME): Appreciated. Also can you add a note in billing console UX that shows "expected refill at 00:00 local time (may take up to 5 minutes to fully clear rate limits)"? That would prevent a lot of confusion.

Maya (Support): Noted — filing a billing-console UX ticket and tagging Raj. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Raj (Billing): Filed: ticket #BILL-4927 — add refill propagation note to billing UI.

Lina (eng-oncall): I'll run a small canary tomorrow around 23:45 PT to verify the cache fix. Will update here once complete.

John (ACME): Sounds good — thanks all for the quick help.
